meanings.note: Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？

meanings.en: from now on; in the future; now
meanings.note: Time expression referring to the immediate or upcoming future.

examples.text: これから家へ帰ります。

examples.trans: The real test starts from here.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.
So, what was it you wanted to consult me about?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: もう別現場で仕事し始めてるよ。監督とメイクの仕事も少しずつ増えてきたし。
examples.trans: I've already started working on other sets, and directing and makeup jobs are picking up.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Used as a noun or adverbially to mean 'for life / forever'.

examples.trans: I will never forget it for the rest of my life.

examples.text: これは一生の思い出です。

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Standard heartfelt apology.

examples.text: ごめんなさい、もうしません。
examples.trans: I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

examples.trans: This man is an ex-convict! He will stain our group's businesses!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Expresses frustration, regret, or surprise that reality contradicts what was expected; often trails off at the end of a spoken complaint.

examples.text: 約束したのに来なかった。
examples.trans: Even though they promised, they did not come.

examples.text: せっかくの休みなのに。
examples.trans: Even though it is a hard-earned day off.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

examples.trans: I work to support my family.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

meanings.en: bad; sorry (in past 悪かった)
meanings.note: Casual past 悪かったな admits fault ('that was bad of me / my bad').

examples.text: 今日は天気が悪いです。

meanings.note: Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: 買えます is the polite potential form meaning 'can buy / can afford to buy'.

examples.text: 本屋で雑誌を買いました。
examples.trans: I bought a magazine at the bookstore.

examples.text: この値段なら買えますよ。
examples.trans: At this price, we can buy it.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
